summary: Both reports satisfy the eight-H2 structure and most checked claims, numbers, affiliations, status labels, resource boundaries, and figure captions, but publication remains blocked by one central STU scope reversal and one non-exact equation transcription.

constraints.sourceMode: fixed local captures and source manifest

reportLocation.excerpt: 这里的正类包括‘挡路障碍’，并不只包含未知语义类

findings.finding: The sentence reverses the checked evaluation scope. TriO's combined evaluation keeps ground negatives from the two naturalistic train sequences and positive obstacle points from STU validation; STU defines those validation targets as OOD anomalies intentionally disjoint from inlier/training classes. The model output is obstacle/ground rather than an anomaly-membership score, but the evaluated positive labels are still the STU anomaly objects. The current wording implies known semantic obstacles are also positive examples in this evaluation, which the sources do not support.

evidence.note: TriO keeps only ground negatives from train and obstacle positives from validation.
STU defines outliers as OOD/anomalous elements and distinguishes them from inlier classes.

findings.requiredFix: State that TriO predicts obstacle-versus-ground rather than semantic novelty, while this reported evaluation's positives are STU anomaly obstacles and its negatives are ground-only. Preserve the warning that the AP is not directly comparable to standard STU point-level anomaly AP or the hidden test benchmark.

findings.finding: The report introduces this as the paper's Eq. 2 but drops the overbar from the left-hand side. The primary source is exactly \bar{S}_e(u), not S_e(u). Because the report explicitly claims an exact equation transcription, the notation should match the source.
findings.requiredFix: Change the displayed left-hand side to \bar{S}_e(u), or explicitly state that S_e is a deliberate local renaming instead of presenting it as the source equation verbatim.

trio-trimodal-anything-perception: Authors and union of affiliations match the v1 author block: Waabi and University of Toronto.
ECCV 2026 poster record exists and the project page labels the paper Spotlight; no specific 2026 proceedings chapter or standalone DOI was verified in the inspected captures.
Exactly two internal count contradictions are preserved: STU 22 versus 2 train plus 19 validation, and AV2 700 train versus 750 train; both retain 150 validation.
AV2 and STU configurations contain no radar; the tri-modal radar results are tied to unreleased LRR.
STU uses one LiDAR and one front camera, z in [-3,5] m, front-camera projection, time zero queries, occupancy below 0.5 mapped to ground, and an evaluation-set F1-maximizing operating threshold.
Table 2 values 74.8/72.9, 76.1/50.3, and 81.6/54.9/77.7/71.3 match the primary source.
AV2 L1/NFCD, LRR long-range numbers, radar ablations, and the 2,280/19 LRR sequence scope match the source.
Table 10 planner-query comparison correctly distinguishes full TriO from TriO without camera: 489.32 versus 60.81 ms and 9,915 versus 3,449 MB on RTX 5000 with 20,000 queries.
Failure claims for exhaust, snow, tangential flow, occupancy-flow inconsistency, and foam-pool-noodle false negative are present in the source.
Project and arXiv captures did not expose an official TriO code/config/weights release; the report correctly limits that claim to the inspected resources.
metric-validity-driving-execution: Authors, affiliations, v1 submission date, preprint status, and CC0 license match the primary source and arXiv capture.
NAVSIM, NAVSIM-v2, and World Engine comparison rows match each related work's own primary text.
The matched NR WorldEngine interface reversal is reported on the correct endpoint; NoRD and TOAD are retained as counterexamples.
All Table 4 deltas and interaction intervals match, including the three reversals and positive gains for NoRD and TOAD under both interfaces.
The 288-scene, 1,152-score-per-family, 576-initial-plan-pair scope, eight updates at 0.5 s over four seconds, fixed settings, and 2,000-draw statistical procedures match the source.
The 0.14% comfort-failure rate and nuPlan CLS/jerk changes match the source and are properly kept separate from the main interface reversal.

NAVSIM-v2 is correctly described as a 450-original/5,462-synthetic re-inference with no LiDAR in synthetic assets; the three free-form combined changes include zero, while NoRD is +0.079 [0.048,0.112].
The fixed-first-plan Qwen-Drive control is correctly reported as playback-minus-LQR -0.005 [-0.035,0.024] and not used as an additive causal decomposition.
Playback is correctly framed as a comparison interface rather than a physical gold standard, and the report avoids real-world transfer claims.
The arXiv abstract and fixed v1 did not expose a dedicated audit repository or complete release package; the report's resource statement is properly scoped to those inspected pages.

figures.captionCorrespondence: Shows LiDAR, RADAR, and camera inputs; LiDAR/RADAR and image backbones; voxel/deformable attention; implicit decoder; occupancy, segmentation, and flow outputs; and future LiDAR, segmentation mask, and radar velocity pseudo-labels.

Three panels show the road image, rendered depth, and obstacle segmentation; low foam-pool-noodle-like objects remain ground-colored in the segmentation. The raw JPEG omits the HTML figure's overlaid A marker, as the report discloses.
Panel (a) is conceptual; panel (b) is the nonlinear human-normalized radial display of score components and behavioral diagnostics with axes oriented outward as better.
Camera and BEV panels depict DiffusionDrive, DiffusionDriveV2, and Human; visible labels are 0.09/0.874, 1.74/0.979, and 0.10/0.878, matching the report.

limitations: This is a source-and-artifact audit, not a reproduction of training, inference, planners, rendering, or datasets.
The review used the fixed local captures declared in the source manifest; it did not refresh the web during this reviewer pass.
The verdict remains same-family provisional per the requested reviewer configuration.
